detail.longDescription: I am trying to create a virtual environment for a Python project to be deployed in a Docker container. I have two versions of Python installed on my Windows11. I have 3.13.15 installed with anaconda3, and I also installed pythoncore-3.14-64 independently of anaconda3. When I create the virtual environment for my project ( python -m venv .venv ) it uses the path for the Python version installed with anaconda3. I need to learn how to change that and have venv point to Python I installed. In VS Code terminal, when I execute: python -m venv .venv it creates .venv folder and inside that folder pyvenv.cfg file containing the following information. home = C:\Users\<userid>\anaconda3 include-system-site-packages = false version = 3.13.9 executable = C:\Users\<userid>\anaconda3\python.exe command = C:\Users\<userid>\anaconda3\python.exe -m venv C:\Users\<userid>\OneDrive\Projects\pymovies\.venv My problem is that anacond3 Python is not the right version for my project. It generates a huge list (hundreds) of Python package references in requirements.txt file when I execute: pip freeze > requirements.txt I would like to understand why anaconda3 Python is selected and how to change it. It's probably some environment variable that VS Code is using but I couldn't find any information about it. I also need to know how to change the selected Python version. Can I modify the information in pyvenv.cfg manually? What are the unexpected problems if I change pyvenv.cfg directly?
